source.title: A PAC-Bayesian Generalization Bound for Equivariant Networks
source.authors: A. Behboodi; Gabriele Cesa; T. Cohen

record.tranche_reason: The study compares equivariant models trained on original and random labels and reports their generalization errors, using a different architecture and datasets from V1.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports group-size effects, bound-to-error correlations, and bound behavior during training. Those results do not measure a named version's specified behavior, so they are not rows. The cited findings from prior work are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: Section 12.5 repeats the random-label comparison in a new setting: group-equivariant networks on transformed MNIST and synthetic symmetry datasets. It reports chance-level test error and successful random-label fitting for sufficiently large synthetic-data models, with incomplete fitting on larger MNIST training sets.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the random-label subsection, but omits its capacity caveat. The paper's broader conclusion is that equivariance-aware PAC-Bayes bounds provide architectural guidance and correlate with error at fixed training-set size, while failing to capture improvement with larger training sets.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains shallow group-equivariant MLP classifiers, including image models with steerable input filters, on transformed MNIST, CIFAR-10, and synthetic symmetry datasets. It uses Adam without weight decay or additional regularization; the V1 comparison uses different datasets and architectures from the named examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports generalization changing with equivariance group size and training-set size; for random-label comparisons, it uses G-MNIST variations and synthetic datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing the equivariance group generally improves generalization at approximately fixed layer dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matching rotational and reflection symmetries through architectural equivariance can improve generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed PAC-Bayes bound tracks some fixed-training-set comparisons but is generally vacuous and can increase with training-set size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An equivariance-aware PAC-Bayes bound can track architectural differences without accurately predicting absolute error or sample-size effects.

record.problems: Random-label training fit is described qualitatively as occurring for sufficiently large models, without a training-error value. Natural-label test-error values in the random-label comparisons are figure-only. The random-label experiments are on transformed MNIST and synthetic data, not the specific natural-image settings in V1.

untested.parts: The named CIFAR-10 and ImageNet architectures and recipes are not replicated. Exact random-label training errors are not supplied.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison isolating spatial convolution or local connectivity against fully connected image classifiers.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No empirical comparison of magnitude-aware sharpness with generalization gaps or competing measures.
No removal and retraining experiment using memorization-ranked examples.

missing.what: A separate random-label training-fit row for sufficiently large synthetic SO(2) models; the text reports successful fitting without an exact training-error value.
Higher training errors on larger transformed-MNIST training sets, with limited model capacity offered as the authors' explanation. Exact errors and affected configurations are unspecified.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope verdict based on figure-only original-label values: inability to read a result does not demonstrate a failure of the claim. The original-label arms were tested, but their individual outcomes remain unresolved in this text rendering. Deliberately randomizing labels is relevant here because V1 explicitly concerns random-label memorization capacity.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses transformed MNIST and synthetic symmetry datasets, not the specified CIFAR-10 architectures or ImageNet; it does not report a numeric natural-label versus random-label training-error comparison.
